title: Picture-Based General Logical Reasoning (Visual Reasoning)
shortDescription: Counting figures, embedded figures, pattern completion, dice and cubes — beyond mirror/water/paper-folding.
genZNote: No words, just shapes. Counting systematically beats staring — and the painted-cube formula is a free mark.

sections.heading: Counting Figures
bullets: Triangles in a triangle with base divided into n segments joined to apex: n(n + 1)/2.
Squares in an n × n grid: n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 (8 × 8 chessboard → 204).
Rectangles (including squares) in an m × n grid: C(m + 1, 2) × C(n + 1, 2) = [m(m + 1)/2] × [n(n + 1)/2].
Method: count by size/category (single, double, triple, etc.) to avoid missing or repeating.

sections.heading: Dice and Cubes
bullets: Standard dice: opposite faces sum to 7 (1–6, 2–5, 3–4).
Two positions of a die with a common face: the non-common faces are adjacent; use them to find opposite faces.
Painted cube of side n cut into unit cubes: 3 faces painted = 8; 2 faces = 12(n − 2); 1 face = 6(n − 2)²; no face = (n − 2)³.
Example: 4 × 4 × 4 cube → 3 faces: 8; 2 faces: 24; 1 face: 24; 0 faces: 8.

sections.heading: Pattern, Series and Embedded Figures
bullets: Figure series: track rotation (clockwise/anticlockwise, 45°/90°), shifting positions, increasing/decreasing elements, shading and symbol alternation.
Embedded figure: the given shape is hidden inside a complex shape in the same size and orientation.
Figure completion/matrix: rules apply across rows and columns; look at number of elements, shading and lines.
Mirror and water images and paper folding are in the Non-Verbal Reasoning lesson.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Visual reasoning uses systematic counting, dice/cube rules and pattern tracking to solve picture-based problems.

commonTraps: Do not assume dice opposite faces are always 7 — only standard dice.

sources.name: Standard competitive-exam reasoning reference (R.S. Aggarwal, Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning)
